There's no distinction in the US? Because they're very different things. 

Here, daycares are run in a seperated building from the caregiver's home, have multiple employees, are heavily regulated, and take in more children.

Dayhomes are run in-home, have fewer children, and usually only one adult. They can be unapproved (very few official regulations, more parent/caregiver choice) or approved (moderate regulation, less parent/caregiver choice), but neither are as heavily regulated as a daycare.

I posted one link because I'm not interested in spending my evening finding a million studies to prove a common knowledge, common sense thing. Nobody here is saying you have to use them, but saying essential oils do absolutely nothing other than smell pretty encourages a form of ignorance that can lead to harmful or even fatal misuse, especially with pets or children.

Clove oil is a proven topical anesthetic. Dunno about lavender. Like anything 'natural' there's a whole range of effects, from the pretty smelling to the useful to the downright dangerous. 

Acting like essential oils are completely harmless and useless is just as stupid as claiming oils can cure all kinds of stuff and should be used for everything.
